SELECTED_INDEX: 3
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is characteristic of a monosubstituted aromatic ketone.  
• Very strong ring-breathing band of a phenyl group at 1005 cm⁻¹ and companion band at 1033 cm⁻¹ match the typical 1000–1030 cm⁻¹ doublet of monosubstituted benzene rings.  
• Aromatic C=C stretches appear at 1588, 1606 and 1630 cm⁻¹; para- or mono-substituted phenyl rings commonly give intense lines near 1600 cm⁻¹.  
• A conjugated C=O stretch is observed at 1681 cm⁻¹, appropriate for an aryl ketone.  
• CH₃ deformation at 1394 cm⁻¹ and twisting/wagging near 1256–1206 cm⁻¹ indicate a methyl group attached to the carbonyl carbon (acetyl group).  
• C–H stretches at 3065 cm⁻¹ (aromatic) and 2929 cm⁻¹ (aliphatic/methyl) are present.  
Among the candidates, molecule 3 (Cc1ccccc1C=O, acetophenone) uniquely contains a phenyl ring with a single acetyl (–COCH₃) substituent, providing both the required aromatic system and a conjugated carbonyl with a methyl group. Other candidates either lack the phenyl ring, the methyl ketone, or both, making them less consistent with the observed peak pattern.
